items.title: North Korea threatens to close Swiss diplomatic office
items.summary: Such a move would deal a blow to potential efforts by Washington and Seoul to engage Pyongyang through indirect diplomatic channels, experts say.

items.title: Zambia formally indicts opposition leader on treason charges
items.summary: Zambian prosecutors have formally indicted the country's main opposition leader and 12 others on treason charges over an alleged plot to overthrow the government. This comes three months after a contested election which saw incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema secure a second term.

items.title: Zambian opposition leader Mundubile formally indicted on treason charges
items.summary: Zambian prosecutors on Monday formally indicted the country's main opposition leader on treason charges over an alleged plot to overthrow the government.

items.title: From the track to the gallery: Dakar's autumn in the spotlight
items.summary: This November, Dakar hosted two exceptional events: the Youth Olympic Games, which ran until 13 November, and Dak'Art, the Dakar Biennale of contemporary African art, which runs from 19 November to 19 December. The Games were the first Olympic event ever held on the African continent, and the Biennale now brings together artists from across Africa and its diaspora. In this episode, we hear from participants in both events.

items.title: In Abidjan, Africa wants to shape its own demographic future
items.summary: Early in November, Abidjan became the capital of the African demographic debate as the UNFPA, African Union and Côte d'Ivoire led talks on the future of the continent's population.

items.title: After Japan's APEC snub, what's next for its China ties?
items.summary: Japan has long-running concerns over Chinese military expansionism, and Beijing has bristled at Sanae Takaichi's comments on Taiwan. The frosty ties were on full display at the APEC summit.

items.title: EU to impose cap on Chinese hybrid EV imports next month
items.summary: Temporary quotas on vehicles entering the bloc tariff-free will also apply to cars from the UK, Japan and Turkey Business live – latest updates The EU will next month impose its threatened caps on the number of Chinese hybrid cars that can be imported into the bloc without facing a tariff, the European Commission has announced. The quotas will also apply to hybrids from Japan, Turkey, South Korea and the UK, but the principal purpose is to limit imports from China after an agreement with Beijing in October that has led to a rise in exports to the bloc. Continue reading...

items.title: In South Africa, parents' homemade sensory room helps children with ADHD
items.summary: Determined to help their children, parents in a South African township have transformed a discarded shipping container into an underwater-themed sensory room using recycled plastic bottles, cut-out flowers and ferns. Originally designed for children with conditions including ADHD and epilepsy, the space is now benefiting the wider community.

items.title: South African township turns discarded shipping container into community sensory therapy room
items.summary: The initiative, run by non-profit organisation Afrika Tikkun in partnership with Sensory-Space, relies on recycled materials and community participation to provide accessible support where professional therapy services are limited.

items.title: DR Congo and Kenya agree to restore ties
items.summary: After years of strained relations over the conflict in eastern Congo, Kinshasa and Nairobi are moving towards a diplomatic reset. DR Congo's President Felix Tshisekedi met his Kenyan counterpart William Ruto over the weekend and they agreed to to restore normal ties and deepen economic and regional cooperation. Emmet Livingstone reports.

items.title: Tshisekedi and Ruto meet in Congo-Brazzaville to resolve DR Congo-Kenya rift
items.summary: DRC President Félix Tshisekedi met his Kenyan counterpart William Ruto during a mini summit hosted in Congo-Brazzaville on Sunday. The two leaders pledged further relations after years of tensions over the DRC-Rwanda crisis.

items.title: Japan’s Leader, in Break with U.S., Defends International Criminal Court
items.summary: Sanae Takaichi welcomed the court’s president and vowed to accelerate financial support despite an effort by the Trump administration to cripple the global body.

items.title: Takaichi moves up ICC financial support in first meeting with court chief since U.S. sanctions
items.summary: The prime minister said Japan would make its contribution ahead of schedule in her first face-to-face meeting with the ICC president since January.

items.title: Catherine, Princess of Wales, Documents Life With Cancer in BBC Film
items.summary: “Cancer does change you,” Catherine, who is in remission, says in a trailer for the film. It will be released this month.

items.title: Prince and Princess of Wales in Mumbai for Earthshot Prize 2026: All you need to know
items.summary: The sixth Earthshot Prize, founded by Britain’s Prince William to promote innovative climate change solutions, will be presented in Mumbai on November 17, 2026

items.title: India's 'cockroach' party leader says he was stopped from flying to UK
items.summary: Saurav Das said that immigration authorities at Delhi airport told him that his passport had been "flagged".

items.title: Leader of India’s Cockroach movement says he was stopped from boarding flight to UK
items.summary: Saurav Das was due to give talks at UK universities on protest movement but says ‘coward government’ prevented him flying A leader of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement has said he was prevented from leaving Delhi to fly to the UK to give talks on the viral group’s protests. Saurav Das, 27, has been at the forefront of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP), which has amassed millions of social media followers since its launch in May . Das, who was due to fly out early on Tuesday, said immigration officials told him at the airport that his passport had been flagged. Continue reading...

items.title: Death Toll From Indonesia Factory Fire Rises to 26 With Dozens Unaccounted for
items.summary: As the death toll rose to 26, one rescue worker said that more victims might be found near a stairwell in the building. The police opened a criminal investigation.

items.title: 24 Killed After Fire Rips Through Candy Factory in Indonesia
items.summary: Hundreds of people were at the compound when a blaze broke out on Saturday and then raged for hours.

items.title: Deadly fire at confectionery factory kills 24 as rescuers search for dozens still missing
items.summary: A deadly fire that tore through a confectionery factory in Indonesia has claimed the lives of 24 people, with 34 others still missing.

items.title: Indonesia: Search continues for workers trapped after deadly factory fire
items.summary: The death toll from a devastating fire at a confectionery factory west of Jakarta has risen to 26. Rescue workers continue searching for victims trapped beneath the rubble.

items.title: At least 24 people killed in Indonesia factory fire, police say
items.summary: Dozens of employees are still reported to be missing after a blaze broke out at a candy factory in Banten province at around 4:30 pm local time on Saturday.

items.title: Indonesia: Search continues for workers trapped after deadly factory fire
items.summary: The death toll from a devastating fire at a confectionery factory west of Jakarta has risen to 26. Rescue workers continue searching for victims trapped beneath the rubble.

items.title: U.S. targets chip smuggling to China after Huang's return to scandal-hit Nvidia
items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned over extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, linked to Singapore-based company Megaspeed International, who is suspected of being a Chinese spy

items.title: U.S. blacklists Megaspeed after Nvidia spy scandal
items.summary: In a filing Monday, the Commerce Department moved to add the company established by Chinese spy suspect Alice Huang to its so-called entity list.
